editorial:
West of the Divide is a 1934 western directed by Robert N. Bradbury. The Internet Archive item (uploaded by RetroFlixUploads on December 23, 2023) lists a date of 1934-02-15. That is the uploader's metadata. We did not verify it as a release or copyright date. The Internet Archive describes the plot this way: Ted Hayden impersonates a wanted man and joins Gentry's gang, only to learn later that Gentry killed his father.

We could not confirm the film's US public domain status. We did not find the original 1934 copyright registration or notice. We did not read the 1961 renewal listings verbatim, and we did not read the 1962 renewal section. We therefore give no negative renewal finding, and the renewal search is not done. We also did not check the story source, the music cues or the trademark position, so those layers stay undetermined. Before reuse, finish the renewal search by hand in the 1961 and 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion picture volumes. The Copyright Office online records start in 1978 and do not cover these renewals. Also check music and cue-sheet material and any added material in the copy you use.
faq: Can I use clips from West of the Divide in a commercial video?

We cannot say yet. The renewal search is incomplete. We did not read the 1961 renewal listings verbatim and did not read the 1962 renewal section. We also did not find the original 1934 registration or notice. Complete the search and check the music, the story source and any added material in your copy before you rely on it. The Internet Archive's public domain label comes from the uploader and is not a clearance.
Does a performer's name or likeness restrict reuse?

This dossier does not resolve that. Copyright expiry on a film does not remove any right of publicity or trademark claim over a performer's name or image. We did not research the point, so treat it as unresolved if you use a performer's name in marketing.
